tooltip.trainees.che_book.title: §lChemistry · Trainees - Elective Module 1
tooltip.trainees.che_book.context:
§l§e119 Pullium (Ji)§r§7: Solid silvery metal with a pale gold sheen. Density 8.0 g/cm³, melting point 20°C, boiling point 550°C. Alkali metal. Valence electron configuration [Og] 8s¹. Common oxidation state +1. Electronegativity 0.7, first ionization energy 350 kJ/mol, electron affinity 40 kJ/mol. Highly radioactive, α/β decay, very short half-life. In-game: Kun Nugget and its compounds.
§l§e117 Inversine (Bp)§r§7: Solid black or dark gray non-metal powder. Density 9.5 g/cm³, melting point 350°C, boiling point 500°C. Halogen. Diatomic molecule Bp₂. Valence electron configuration [Lv] 7s²7p⁵. Common oxidation states -1, +1, +3, +5, +7. Electronegativity 2.6, first ionization energy 800 kJ/mol, electron affinity 200 kJ/mol. Highly radioactive, α decay, very short half-life. In-game: Black Powder (Bp₂) and its compounds.
§l§eIonic Compound Pullium Inverside (JiBp)§r§7: White solid (salt-like). In-game, it's a throwable item. On contact with water or impact, it dissociates into Ji⁺ and Bp⁻ ions. Bp⁻ is biologically toxic (similar to cyanide), causing Instant Damage (potion effect).
   §7Both are superheavy elements, highly radioactive, with densities far exceeding their lighter group counterparts. Pullium readily loses one electron—a powerful reducing agent. Inversine readily gains one electron—a powerful oxidizing agent with high electron affinity. Pullium exhibits only +1. Inversine, like Astatine (At), has multiple positive oxidation states but takes -1 when reacting with Pullium.
§r§f  Compounds: Pullium Hydroxide (JiOH), Hydrogen Inverside (HBp), Pullium Inverside (JiBp, craftable into Anti-basketballs), Dipullium Oxide (Ji₂O).
  §l2Ji + 2H₂O → 2JiOH + H₂↑§r (exothermic, explosive, luminous—DANGER!)
  §l2Bp₂ + 2H₂O → 4HBp + O₂↑§r (exothermic, slower reaction)
  §lJi + ½Bp₂ → JiBp§r (highly exothermic, violent explosion, luminous—EXTREME DANGER!!)
  §lJiOH + HBp → JiBp + H₂O§r (highly exothermic, violent reaction—CAUTION)
  §l2Ji + O₂ (ignite) → Ji₂O§r (exothermic—CAUTION)
§7Note: 1. All exothermic reactions, luminescence, and gas production are abstracted in-game. Explosions are represented by TNT logic with equivalent effects. 2. Both substances are radioactive, but radioactivity is abstracted in-game. 3. All values are approximate. §0§r
